title: Special Hours on Google Business Profile: Set Holiday Opening Times
description: How to set special hours, public holidays and closures on your Google Business Profile, when to use "temporarily closed" and mistakes that confuse customers.

answer.question: How do I set holiday hours on my Google Business Profile?
answer.text: Go to your Business Profile, click Edit profile, open Hours and, next to "Special hours", choose Edit. Select the holiday date, untick "Closed" if you open and enter the time slot, or leave it ticked if you close, then save. According to Google's official help, each special hours entry covers a maximum of 24 hours and a one-off closure can last up to six days in a row; if you close for seven or more, use "temporarily closed".

intro: Few things annoy a customer more than turning up at a closed business when Google said it was open. With Christmas and the long weekends close, here is how to set up your profile's special hours step by step and without mistakes.

body.question: How do I set holiday hours on my Google Business Profile?
body.text: Go to your Business Profile, click Edit profile, open Hours and, next to "Special hours", choose Edit. Select the holiday date, untick "Closed" if you open and enter the time slot, or leave it ticked if you close, then save. According to Google's official help, each special hours entry covers a maximum of 24 hours and a one-off closure can last up to six days in a row; if you close for seven or more, use "temporarily closed".
Why holiday hours matter more than they seem

When someone searches "hair salon open today" or "restaurant near me" and finds your profile, the first thing they check is whether you are open. If Google says you open on the afternoon of 24 December and your shutters are down, that person is left standing at the door, annoyed and, if you are lucky, does not leave you a negative review for it. It is one of the cheapest mistakes to avoid and one of the ones that creates the most friction with customers.

Public holidays, long weekends, summer breaks or a closure for refurbishment are normal for any business in Valencia. What is not normal is letting your profile tell a different story from reality. This guide explains how to set special hours, when to use each option and how to build a review routine that takes ten minutes a quarter.
Special hours, regular hours and "temporarily closed": what each one is

Google Business Profile offers several tools and it is best not to mix them up. According to Google's official documentation (Business Profile Help, "Set special hours"), special hours are for short-term changes, such as holidays or one-off events, without touching your regular hours.

items: Regular hours: the ones for every week. If you change permanently (for example, you stop opening on Mondays), you change them here.
Special hours: specific exceptions with a date, such as 1 January, a long weekend or the day of a fair. They disappear from your profile on their own once the date passes.
More hours: different time slots for services within the same day, for example order pickup, home delivery or breakfast time in a café.

Temporarily closed: for long closures or ones of uncertain length. Google says that if you will be closed for seven or more days in a row, or do not know for how long, you should mark the business as temporarily closed instead of using special hours.

body.title: A detail that is easy to miss
body.text: Special hours only show if your hours are set to "Open with main hours". If another option is selected, your holidays will not appear even though you saved them. It is the most common reason behind "I set it and it does not show up".
Step by step: how to add a holiday or a closure

The process on a computer is the same one Google describes in its official help. On mobile, with the profile managed in Google Maps or in Search, the menus have slightly different names, but the logic is identical.

items: Go to your Business Profile with the account that manages it and choose "Edit profile".
Go to the "Hours" section and, in the opening hours area, click "Edit" next to "Special hours".
Choose the date: you can confirm one of those Google suggests or add a custom one.
If you close that day, leave the "Closed" box ticked. If you open, untick it and enter the opening and closing times.
If you open in two shifts (morning and afternoon, like many shops and clinics), use "More" and "Add hours" to enter both slots.
Save the changes and check how the profile looks by searching for your business from another device.

body.text: Two limits that Google states explicitly: each special hours entry cannot exceed 24 hours, and one-off closures cover a maximum of six consecutive days. If you open past midnight, like a bar or a club, Google recommends splitting the hours across two dates: one ending at 24:00 and another starting at 00:00 the next day. Be careful, because the special hours replace the regular ones for that second day and you will have to re-enter any hours you want to keep.
Which dates to check during the year

There is no need to guess: for official holidays, the reliable source is the working calendar published by the Spanish Government and the Generalitat Valenciana, plus the local holidays set by your town hall. Local holidays change from one city to another and from one year to the next, so do not take them for granted. Google recommends confirming the hours for official holidays even if they match your regular hours, because that makes it clear on your profile that you have checked.

items: Christmas, Christmas Eve, New Year's Eve, New Year's Day and Epiphany (6 January).
Easter and any long weekends that fall in your calendar.
Local holidays in your municipality and festivals that affect your area, such as Las Fallas if your business is in Valencia city and you change hours or close.
Summer holidays or an annual closure for rest.
Your own events: stocktaking, refurbishment, team training or an extra opening for a campaign.

body.text: Practical examples by type of business

Hair salon: closes on the afternoon of 24 December but opens in the morning. Set a special entry for the 24th with a single time slot and another for the 31st. If a voucher campaign in December extends opening to 21:00 on Thursdays, that is also a dated special entry, not a change to regular hours.

Restaurant: serves lunch on 1 January but no dinner. Enter the special hours with the midday slot. If it offers home delivery in a different time window from the dining room, use "More hours" so the customer sees each service separately and does not have to call.

Clinic or practice: regional and local holidays affect the diary. A special hours entry stops patients calling the clinic's number with no answer, and avoids misunderstandings with anyone trying to book. It is a good idea to announce the holiday closure by phone and on your website too.

Garage: closed from 1 to 15 August. That is more than six days, so it does not fit in special hours: the right thing is to use the "temporarily closed" status for the duration of the closure and reopen the profile when you are back.
When to touch your profile: a reasonable lead time

Google's official help does not state how far in advance special hours can be scheduled, so there is no universal rule. In practice, a good habit is to load the dates for the next holiday period as soon as you finish the previous one, and to check your profile a week before each long weekend. That way you avoid improvising in a rush and get used to it being a regular task, like cleaning the shop.
If you have several locations: copying hours

In January 2025 Google added a "copy hours" feature to apply the special hours of one location to others you manage, as reported by Search Engine Roundtable. Copied hours replace any the other locations already had, so check before confirming. If you manage many profiles, Google's help also describes bulk upload via spreadsheet, with dates in YYYY-MM-DD format and an "x" to mark an all-day closure. When updating existing profiles this way, include only the columns you need, because an empty column can wipe data that is already saved.
Google can also change your hours

Google has explained that it uses machine learning models to detect hours that are probably wrong and update them automatically, relying on signals such as when the profile was last edited, the hours of nearby businesses, popular times or Street View photos of the hours on the door (Search Engine Land reported this announcement). The recommendation is clear: do not let your profile go stale, review your hours regularly and correct anything that does not match reality.

body.title: Consistency across all channels
body.text: When you update your hours, say the same thing everywhere: your Google profile, your website, your social media and a sign on the door. If every channel says something different, customers do not know which one to believe and trust suffers.
Common mistakes to avoid

items: Changing the regular hours for a holiday and forgetting to put them back. For anything one-off, use special hours.
Leaving the business as open when you have been closed for weeks for refurbishment: for long closures, "temporarily closed" is the right option.
Not checking local holidays, which differ in each municipality.
Setting a special entry while the main hours are on another option, so it never shows.
Forgetting that special hours after midnight replace those of the following day.

body.text: Quarterly review checklist

body.title: Before every long weekend or campaign
items: You open your profile and check that the regular hours are the real ones today.
You have checked the working calendar and the local holidays for the coming quarter.
You have loaded a special entry for every date on which you change hours or close.
Closures of seven days or more are marked as "temporarily closed".
Your website, social media and signage say the same as your profile.
You have searched for your business on mobile to check how a customer sees it.

body.text: What to do from now on

Do a check today: search for your business on Google from your phone and see which hours appear for the coming holidays. If something does not add up, fix it following the steps above. It is a small, free improvement that customers notice. faq.q: Can I schedule Christmas hours months in advance?
faq.a: Google's official help does not say how far in advance special hours can be set, so the prudent approach is to load them as the dates get closer and check they show correctly on your profile. The important thing is not to wait until the same day.

faq.q: What is the difference between special hours and temporarily closed?
faq.a: Special hours are for short changes with a date, such as a holiday; Google says they cover closures of up to six days in a row. If you close for seven days or more, or do not know how long it will last, you should mark the profile as temporarily closed.

faq.q: I set special hours and they do not show on my profile. Why?
faq.a: According to Google, special hours only show if your hours are set to "Open with main hours". Check that option and also make sure the date and times were saved.

faq.q: Can I show different hours for delivery or pickup?
faq.a: Yes. Google offers "More hours" for services with different time slots, such as home delivery, pickup or breakfast, so the customer sees each set of hours separately.

faq.q: Can Google change my hours without telling me?
faq.a: Google has explained that it uses machine learning to update hours it considers probably incorrect. That is why it is worth reviewing your profile regularly and correcting anything that does not match reality.

faq.q: I have several premises. Do I have to enter holidays one by one?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Google lets you copy special hours from one location to others and also offers bulk upload via spreadsheet. Check before applying, because copied hours replace existing ones.
